claims.text: Claim: both goods and services consumer spending rose in Q1 2024. The BEA second estimate confirms consumer spending rose overall and drove the GDP revision, but it does not provide a goods-versus-services breakdown in the supplied excerpts, so the claim cannot be fully verified from these sources.

citations.quotation: The GDP estimate for the first quarter was revised down 0.3 percentage point from the “advance” estimate, primarily reflecting a downward revision to consumer spending.

the deceleration in real GDP in the first quarter primarily reflected decelerations in consumer spending, exports, and state and local government spending and a downturn in federal government spending.

counterarguments.text: The provided excerpts do not disaggregate consumer spending into goods and services; a downward revision to consumer spending suggests at least part of spending was weaker than first estimated, which is contrary to an unqualified 'both rose' claim.

citations.quotation: primarily reflecting a downward revision to consumer spending

limitations: The supplied excerpts contain no goods vs. services breakdown of consumer spending, so the claim that both rose cannot be confirmed or refuted from these sources alone.
The second estimate is not final; the third estimate was scheduled for June 27, 2024.
The 1.3 percent figure is an annualized rate for real GDP; it is not evidence about price-adjusted vs. nominal components beyond what is stated.
Publication date (2024-05-30) is declared, not independently verified; excerpts are partial coverage of the full release.

citation.quotation: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.3 percent in the first quarter of 2024, according to the “second” estimate.
In the fourth quarter of 2023, real GDP increased 3.4 percent.
The GDP estimate for the first quarter was revised down 0.3 percentage point from the “advance” estimate
